reason: The bone-lineage environment is shown directing stem-cell descendants toward bone-related activity, so this is a clear starting point for living bone.
expectation: The stem-cell descendants will develop into bone-lineage cells.

alternatives.reason: The membrane looks like it could line the sleeve, but I chose to start with the bone cells.

effect: The lineage produced bone-matrix-making cells and embedded bone cells, giving me a living component for the bone.
reaction: The distinction between cells that produce matrix and cells embedded in it is interesting.
reason: The picture places bone cells in mature bone, and the collagen framework outlines the same arm bones, so I’ll try bringing them together.
expectation: The bone cells will become part of the collagen framework.

alternatives.reason: The mineral is also shown within the same bone outlines and might strengthen the framework.

effect: The bone framework now includes cells, while its mineral and blood-supply details remain to be added.
reaction: The cutaway makes it clear that these are parts of existing mature bones, not a new bone growing instantly.
reason: The mineral was pictured in the same bone outlines, and the framework still lacks its mineral detail.
expectation: The mineral will be added to the bone framework with cells.

alternatives.reason: The membrane appears to fit the sleeve's unlined inner face, but I’ll continue building the bones first.

effect: The bone cutaway now includes mineral, collagen and cells, but its blood-vessel detail is still unfilled.
reaction: The remaining vessel outline makes the next step clear.
reason: Blood vessels were pictured in the same arm-bone outlines, and the goal calls for supplied bones.
expectation: The blood vessels will complete the bone's blood-supply detail.

effect: The arm bones now have cells, mineral and a blood supply; the new goal is to connect them into a supported joint.
reaction: Seeing the different bone components together makes their roles clearer.
reason: The synovial membrane is described as a lining, and the fibrous sleeve has an unlined inner face, matching the capsule goal.
expectation: The membrane will line the inside of the joint sleeve.

effect: The sleeve is now lined, completing the capsule goal; the bones still need to be connected into a supported, movable joint.
reaction: The lining and its fluid make the capsule’s purpose clearer.
reason: The cartilage is shown as smooth caps, so I expect it to fit over the bone ends where they meet.
expectation: The cartilage will cover the arm bones’ joint surfaces.

alternatives.reason: The capsule also belongs around the elbow, but the cartilage seems useful to add to the bone ends first.

effect: The bone ends now have smooth cartilage surfaces that can slide against each other; the joint still needs its capsule and support.
reaction: The sliding inset makes the cartilage’s role clear.
reason: The capsule surrounds the elbow’s bone ends, so it should fit around the cartilage-covered bones.
expectation: The lined capsule will surround the joint between the bones.

alternatives.reason: The ligaments also span the elbow and could provide support.

effect: The capsule now encloses the cartilage-covered bone ends, with fluid helping the surfaces glide. The joint still needs support.
reaction: The cutaway makes the lining and fluid’s role clearer.
reason: The elbow ligaments are shown spanning the joint, so they should provide the remaining support.
expectation: The ligaments will reinforce the enclosed elbow while allowing it to move.

effect: The ligaments completed the joint, showing how it can bend while resisting sideways movement. All chapter goals are complete.
reaction: The bending and sideways-resistance arrows made the ligaments’ role clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Putting the cartilage, capsule and ligaments together was most worthwhile because the cutaways showed how the elbow can glide and stay supported.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the bone components one at a time felt a little repetitive, although the pictures showed what each added.

surprise.text: I was surprised that bone cells can become embedded in the material they produce, with tiny channels connecting their spaces.

arbitrary.text: None felt especially arbitrary: the pictures and goals generally made the pairings clear. The names osteoblast and osteocyte were new, but their roles were labeled.

continue.text: I would choose to try another chapter: seeing the separate bone and joint parts come together made me curious about how muscles would move the arm. Some of the individual assembly steps were predictable, though.
